goal: Define the spio package-manager product contract with security, resolution, cache, concurrency, error-handling, workflow, IDE, and platform requirement labels in Requirements.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/package-manager-roadmap/Requirements.md only. Context: the existing repository-delivery-convergence plan consolidates planning signals but defines no product contract, while the 2026-07-11 audit confirmed P0 security gaps (native registry fetch verifies only a root.json SHA-256 pin with no Ed25519 TUF chain while the Python validator implements the full chain; trust descriptor import stores pins without signature or expiry enforcement; the control-plane publish endpoint is unauthenticated and accepts arbitrary host paths), P1 robustness gaps (git snapshot tar extraction without prescan, PATH-resolved curl/git/tar subprocesses, no inter-process locking on SPIO_HOME, non-atomic lockfile writes), and structural facts (exact-version-only single-version-v1 resolver, POSIX-only process layer); upstream SymPolicy/Pafio already drafted a package-manager-roadmap with REQ-SEC/WF/IDE/CACHE/WS labels plus SecurityAudit.md AUD-2026-07-001..010 that downstream never absorbed. Target: a downstream Requirements.md defining REQ-SEC-001 native TUF chain parity, REQ-SEC-002 control-plane authentication and publish path confinement, REQ-SEC-003 archive extraction prescan parity for all acquisition paths, REQ-SEC-004 trust descriptor signature and expiry enforcement, REQ-SEC-005 absolute-path subprocess invocation, REQ-CON-001 inter-process cache/lockfile/trust-store locking, REQ-ERR-001 atomic state writes and failure-recovery error taxonomy, REQ-RES-001 resolver contract closure (exact-version policy decision, cycle detection, conflict diagnostics), REQ-CACHE-001 content-addressed store completion and offline vendoring, REQ-WF-001 build/run/test receipts, REQ-IDE-001 Vityo machine-payload emission, REQ-PLAT-001 platform matrix decision (Windows scope); each with users, scope, non-goals, and measurable acceptance targets. Design Considerations: adopt upstream label families where re-verified downstream and add REQ-CON/REQ-ERR because concurrency and atomicity findings are downstream-confirmed but unlabeled upstream; security requirements state the exact trust boundary each defends. Design Value: converts the flat 71-signal backlog into a labeled product contract with priority semantics (P0 security first). Constraints & Risks: must respect the frozen CLI contract (docs/governance/Spio-CLI-Contract.md), the local-first independence rules in README.md, and the OSS boundary that rejects private auth hooks in the open tree.

goal: Record the spio module map, trust boundaries, new security/concurrency module contracts, and per-node file ownership in Architecture.md.
description: Scope: docs/plan/package-manager-roadmap/Architecture.md only. Context: the native tree already layers cleanly (spio executable -> spio_cli_shell -> spio_cli_commands -> project/package/toolchain services -> spio_resolution -> spio_manifest -> spio_foundation, with all subprocesses through SpioCore/Process), but the security fixes need new shared components that multiple nodes will consume: a native TUF verification module, a signed trust-descriptor format, a file-locking primitive, an atomic-write helper, and a shared archive-prescan routine currently owned by the registry client only. Target: Architecture.md records (1) the current module/target map with one responsibility per library, (2) trust-boundary placement: which module enforces which guarantee (SpioSecurity owns TUF chain + descriptor signatures; SpioCore owns Process hardening, Sha256, new FileLock and AtomicFile; extraction prescan moves to a shared SpioSecurity routine consumed by both registry and git paths), (3) interface contracts for the new components (verify_tuf_chain(metadata_set) -> verified targets, FileLock::acquire(path, scope), AtomicFile::write(path, bytes), PrescanArchive(listing) -> confined paths), (4) dependency direction proving no new upward dependencies (services depend on SpioSecurity/SpioCore, never the reverse), and (5) per-implementation-node file ownership showing parallel nodes stay disjoint, with explicit sequencing where nodes share files (Resolver.cpp is touched by both the git-prescan and resolver nodes; Client.cpp by TUF and cache nodes). Design Considerations: reuse the Python verifier's verification order as the reference algorithm for the native port; locking granularity is per-store (cache, trust, project lockfile), not one global lock; keep the CLI layer contract-frozen. Design Value: prevents five security nodes from each inventing their own primitives and keeps the fix surface reviewable. Constraints & Risks: POSIX-only Process layer bounds what FileLock can promise on Windows (record the decision under REQ-PLAT-001); no OpenSSL-style heavyweight dependency without a recorded decision (Ed25519 verify can come from a minimal vetted implementation).

goal: Port full TUF chain verification (root -> timestamp -> snapshot -> targets, Ed25519) into the native registry client so forged metadata fails closed.
description: Scope: src/SpioSecurity (new native TUF verifier module per Architecture.md), src/SpioRegistryClient/Client.cpp metadata consumption (~753-805), and native tests with adversarial fixtures; the Python validator (src/spio_registry_v2/validator.py) is the reference algorithm and stays authoritative for publisher-side checks. Context: the native fetch path currently verifies only a SHA-256 pin of trust/root.json before consuming index and artifact metadata, so any attacker who can serve registry objects (or poison a mirror) can forge snapshot/timestamp/targets without the native client noticing, while the Python verifier (~182-404) implements the full signed chain with role thresholds and expiry; this is the audit's P0-1 (upstream AUD-2026-07-001). Target: MaterializeRegistryPackage and every native metadata consumer verify the complete chain (signature thresholds per role, version monotonicity, expiry windows, hash links from snapshot to targets to artifacts) before trusting any object, with verification failures producing stable error codes and no partial cache writes; tampering with any role file in fixtures must fail the fetch. Design Considerations: port the Python verifier's order and checks exactly (parity fixtures shared between both implementations); Ed25519 verification via a minimal vetted implementation recorded in Architecture.md rather than a heavyweight TLS library; keep verification pure (bytes in, verdict out) for unit testability; cache verified metadata keyed by digest so re-verification is cheap. Design Value: closes the highest-severity trust gap in the product; parity with the Python verifier turns two half-implementations into one contract with two enforcers. Constraints & Risks: offline mode must still work from previously verified cache; root-key rotation flow must match the descriptor-signing node's format (coordinate via Architecture.md contract); performance of per-fetch verification must stay within the perf gate.

goal: Authenticate the registry control plane and confine publish inputs to a staging directory.
description: Scope: src/spio_registry_v2/registry-v2-control-plane-server.py (~178-210 publish handling), the control-plane client call sites, contracts/registry-control-plane/v1 schema updates, and interop tests; OSS boundary rules apply. Context: the control-plane /publish endpoint currently accepts unauthenticated requests carrying arbitrary archive_path/manifest_path values, so any local or network peer can publish packages or exfiltrate host files by pointing the server at them (audit P0-3, upstream AUD mapping; April 2026 audit item SPIO-AUD-014 also flags HTTP 200 on failure). Target: every mutating control-plane endpoint requires a bearer token (mTLS recorded as a deployment option) with constant-time comparison and denied-by-default when unconfigured; publish inputs resolve strictly inside a configured staging directory (reject absolute paths and traversal after canonicalization); failures return correct HTTP status codes with structured JSON errors; auth-negative and traversal-negative interop tests cover both. Design Considerations: token config via environment/file with no default token; path confinement uses resolve-then-prefix-check (the same canonicalization discipline as the archive prescan); keep the read plane static and unauthenticated as designed. Design Value: the control plane is the publish trust root; an unauthenticated one invalidates every downstream signature story. Constraints & Risks: OSS tree must keep private-auth hooks out (SecurityTests enforce this) so the bearer scheme must be the documented open mechanism; localhost-only test harness, no external network.

goal: Extend archive-extraction prescan to the git acquisition path and remove the tar-listing truncation window.
description: Scope: the shared prescan routine placed per Architecture.md (SpioSecurity), its adoption in src/SpioResolve/Resolver.cpp git snapshot extraction (~316-354), the registry path's existing ValidateTarListingPaths call sites in src/SpioRegistryClient/Client.cpp (~643-707), and the tar-listing capture policy in src/SpioCore/Process.hpp (~35-36). Context: registry artifacts are prescanned for path traversal before extraction, but git-sourced snapshots run git archive | tar -xf with no listing validation, so a malicious pinned git dependency can zip-slip or symlink-escape into the workspace (audit P1-1); additionally the prescan reads tar -tf output through a 1 MiB stdout cap, so an archive with a listing larger than the cap could truncate the scan (P2-1). Target: one shared prescan routine validates entry paths (reject absolute, drive-letter, .. traversal, and symlink targets escaping the extraction root after canonicalization) for both registry and git acquisition, with the listing read uncapped (streaming reader or raised bound with explicit overflow failure) so truncation cannot skip entries; extraction proceeds only after a complete, validated listing. Design Considerations: prefer failing closed on listing overflow rather than best-effort scanning; keep the routine pure over the listing text for unit testability; symlink policy is reject-by-default (packages have no legitimate escape use). Design Value: one enforcement point for every archive that enters the machine, closing the acquisition-path asymmetry the audit flagged. Constraints & Risks: git-sourced projects with unusual but legitimate layouts must keep working (fixtures include deep paths and unicode names); performance on large archives must stay within perf-gate bounds.

acceptance_criteria.text: Zip-slip and symlink-escape fixtures fail extraction on the git path with stable errors (native/interop tests).

acceptance_criteria.text: A fixture whose tar listing exceeds the old 1 MiB cap is fully scanned (or fails closed on overflow), proven by test.

goal: Enforce signed, expiring trust descriptors and absolute-path subprocess invocation.
description: Scope: src/SpioSecurity/RegistryTrust.cpp descriptor import (~196-248), the descriptor schema in contracts/registry-v2, subprocess spawn specs in src/SpioCore/Process.hpp (~31 search_path default) and the curl/git/tar call sites in src/SpioRegistryClient/Client.cpp (~381) and src/SpioResolve/Resolver.cpp. Context: trust descriptor import currently stores registry pins without any cryptographic verification and ignores issued_at/expires fields, so an attacker who can hand a user a descriptor file pins a malicious registry root (audit P0-2); separately, external tools are spawned with search_path=true, so a PATH-planted curl/git/tar binary executes with the user's privileges (P1-2). Target: descriptor import verifies an Ed25519 signature over the canonical descriptor bytes against configured signer keys (sharing the crypto primitive from the TUF node via SpioSecurity), enforces expiry and issuance windows with clock-skew tolerance, and rejects unsigned/expired/unknown-signer descriptors with stable errors; tool paths for curl/git/tar resolve once at startup to absolute paths (config override allowed) and all security-relevant spawns set search_path=false. Design Considerations: canonical-bytes signing (exact file bytes, no re-serialization) avoids canonicalization bugs; key configuration lives beside the trust store with a documented rotation flow consistent with the TUF root; tool resolution failure is a startup diagnostic, not a mid-operation surprise. Design Value: closes the descriptor bootstrap hole that would otherwise bypass the entire TUF chain, and removes the PATH-hijack class in one sweep. Constraints & Risks: dev/test flows need a documented way to trust local descriptors (explicit --dev flag with loud warning, never silent); absolute-path resolution must respect the existing SPIO_* env override contract.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unsigned, expired, and unknown-signer descriptor imports are rejected with stable errors (SecurityTests negative cases).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: RegistryTrust.cpp verifies signed envelopes via Ed25519+signer keys, enforces issued_at/expires; unsigned rejected unless --dev; SecurityTests negative cases for expired/unknown-signer/unsigned

acceptance_criteria.text: Security-relevant subprocess spawns use absolute tool paths with search_path=false (code evidence plus a PATH-hijack simulation test that fails to hijack).

goal: Introduce inter-process file locking for SPIO_HOME stores and atomic writes for every mutable state file.
description: Scope: new FileLock and AtomicFile primitives in src/SpioCore per Architecture.md, adoption in cache mutation paths (src/SpioRegistryClient/Client.cpp checkout materialization, src/SpioResolve/Resolver.cpp EnsureCheckout ~712-721 TOCTOU window), trust-store writes (already temp+rename per RegistryTrust.cpp ~91-114, keep), and lockfile writes (src/SpioApp/PackageApp.cpp ~286-297, src/SpioManifest/Dependencies.cpp ~83-95 direct ofstream); interop test for two concurrent spio processes. Context: nothing in src/ takes any inter-process lock, so two concurrent spio invocations (developer shell plus IDE background sync) can interleave cache materialization, tear spio.lock, or race trust-store updates; cache downloads already use temp+rename (Client.cpp ~101-124) but checkout extraction and project lockfiles do not (audit P1-3/P1-4). Target: per-store advisory locks (cache store, trust store, project lockfile scope) acquired for mutation windows with bounded wait and a clear lock-held error path; every mutable state write (spio.lock, spio-toolchain.lock, cache indexes) goes through AtomicFile (same-directory temp, fsync, rename); a two-process interop test proves one winner or a clean lock diagnostic with no torn state. Design Considerations: advisory flock-style locking on POSIX now (REQ-PLAT-001 records the Windows mapping decision); lock ordering documented (project -> cache -> trust) to prevent deadlock; read paths stay lock-free against the immutable content-addressed store. Design Value: concurrency safety is a correctness floor for IDE integration (Vityo triggers background syncs) and costs little on the happy path. Constraints & Risks: NFS/odd-filesystem lock semantics are recorded as a known limitation; crash-while-holding-lock recovery relies on advisory-lock auto-release plus temp-file cleanup on next run.

acceptance_criteria.text: Two parallel spio sync processes over one SPIO_HOME finish with one winner or a clean lock error and byte-consistent stores (interop test).

goal: Close the resolver contract: recorded exact-version policy decision, full cycle detection, and actionable conflict diagnostics.
description: Scope: src/SpioResolve/Resolver.cpp (SingleVersionResolver ~684-786, cycle handling ~765-768), src/SpioManifest/Manifest.cpp version parsing (~131-136), resolver error types in SpioFoundation Errors, and resolver test vectors; documentation of the policy in docs/governance/Spio-Manifest-and-Lock-Conventions.md. Context: the resolver is a deterministic single-version DFS with fingerprint dedup that hard-fails on any same-name version/source divergence, supports exact x.y.z only, and detects self-dependency but not longer cycles; whether to add semver ranges is a product decision with large blast radius (lockfile schema, registry index, IDE payloads), and diamond-conflict errors today do not tell the user which two dependency chains disagree. Context also includes the workspace member model (explicit members/exclude, no globs) that resolution iterates. Target: (1) a recorded policy decision — keep exact-version single-version-v1 as the contract (with rationale: determinism, local-first, small registry) or introduce a bounded range form — written into the conventions doc and mirrored in Requirements.md via the requirements-update flow if it changes scope; (2) full dependency-cycle detection (DFS color marking) with a diagnostic naming the cycle path; (3) conflict diagnostics that print both requirement chains (root -> ... -> name@vA vs root -> ... -> name@vB) so users can fix the right manifest; (4) resolver behavior locked by new test vectors (diamond agreement, diamond conflict, cycle, workspace member overlap). Design Considerations: if ranges are rejected, say so in the error message users hit (expected version format); chain reconstruction can reuse the DFS parent stack with no asymptotic cost; keep resolution deterministic (sorted iteration stays). Design Value: resolver behavior becomes a documented contract with humane failures instead of folklore, without committing to SAT-solver complexity the product does not need. Constraints & Risks: any lockfile schema impact must keep lock-version 1 readers working or record a deliberate version bump through the governance doc; do not change resolution results for currently-valid projects (golden lockfile tests).

acceptance_criteria.text: The version-policy decision is recorded in the conventions doc with rationale, and resolver errors state the expected version format.

goal: Complete the content-addressed store contract: universal digest keying, verified reads, and offline vendoring closure.
description: Scope: src/SpioCore/Paths.cpp store layout, cache read/write paths in src/SpioRegistryClient/Client.cpp (~424-466, ~559-615) and src/SpioResolve/Resolver.cpp GitSourceCache (~64-70, ~194), src/SpioVendor/Vendor.cpp offline flows, and cache tests. Context: registry blobs are already content-addressed (registry/blobs/sha256/xx/yy/digest.tar) with digest verification on fetch, but git checkouts key by FNV-1a64 of the source string plus rev (collision-prone identity, no content digest), extracted checkout trees are not re-verifiable after extraction, and offline mode requires cache-or-vendor without a way to pre-populate the registry cache from a vendored export (REQ-CACHE upstream). Target: every cached artifact class carries a content digest in its metadata (git snapshots gain a recorded tree digest at materialization; FNV keys remain only as directory-name shortcuts, never as identity), cache reads verify digests lazily with a verified-marker to avoid rescan cost, corrupted entries self-heal by refetch (online) or fail with a precise diagnostic (offline), and vendor export/import round-trips registry packages so a vendored project syncs fully offline including registry deps. Design Considerations: digest-verify-on-first-read plus marker matches the perf gate budget; self-heal only deletes provably-corrupt entries (never on IO flakiness — distinguish read errors from digest mismatches); vendor import reuses the same prescan and digest checks as network acquisition. Design Value: makes the cache a trustworthy CAS instead of a best-effort directory tree, which the TUF chain and offline story both depend on. Constraints & Risks: existing caches must migrate lazily (absent metadata treated as unverified, verified on first read) without a flag-day; SPIO_HOME layout is user-visible so directory shape changes need the governance doc updated.

acceptance_criteria.text: Corrupted cache entries are detected on read (digest mismatch), self-heal online, and fail with a precise diagnostic offline (tests for both).
Vendor export/import round-trips registry dependencies so a vendored project syncs fully offline (interop test).
Git snapshot materialization records a content digest and FNV keys are no longer identity-bearing (code evidence plus test).

goal: Emit structured workflow receipts and Vityo machine payloads, and record the platform support matrix decision.
description: Scope: src/SpioApp/WorkflowApp.cpp build/run/test receipt emission, src/SpioResolve/ProjectGraphContract.cpp payload emission (project_graph v1, toolchain_state v1), contracts/ schema files, docs platform-matrix statement, and the cross-repo mirror fixtures consumed by vityo-nightly gates. Context: Vityo currently infers project state from canonical files because spio does not yet emit the machine payloads its own contracts document (this is the supplier side of Vityo REQ-001), workflow commands succeed or fail without machine-readable receipts (REQ-WF upstream: live build/run/test receipts), and the POSIX-only Process layer (fork/exec in src/SpioCore/Process.cpp) leaves Windows support undecided rather than declared (audit P2 platform finding). Target: (1) spio build/run/test emit structured JSON receipts (schema-versioned: phases, exit status, artifact paths, timings) alongside human output, honoring the existing --json conventions; (2) spio project-graph and toolchain-state emit the documented v1 payloads with source-confidence fields, validated against contracts/ schemas in tests and mirrored into the fixture set the Vityo repo consumes; (3) the platform matrix is decided and documented: Linux/macOS native primary, Windows explicitly deferred-with-rationale or scoped via a Process port plan, recorded in README/BUILD docs and the conventions doc. Design Considerations: receipts and payloads are additive surfaces — CLI contract stays frozen for existing flags; schema versioning follows the same major-version fail-closed rule Vityo applies; fixture mirroring uses the existing cross-repo gate scripts rather than manual copies. Design Value: closes the IDE integration loop from the supplier side and turns the platform question from silence into a recorded decision. Constraints & Risks: payload fields must match what resolution actually knows (no invented confidence); Windows decision affects FileLock/Process design and must stay consistent with REQ-CON-001's recorded scope.

acceptance_criteria.text: spio build/run/test emit schema-versioned JSON receipts validated against contracts/ schemas in tests.
project_graph v1 and toolchain_state v1 payloads validate against their schemas and the cross-repo mirror fixtures consumed by vityo-nightly gates are updated.
The platform support matrix decision (Windows scope) is recorded in the governance/build docs consistent with the locking node's scope.

commit.message: workflow: structured receipts, IDE machine payloads, platform matrix decision

goal: Run the full Validation.md matrix including the adversarial security suite on one head commit and prove every requirement label.
description: Scope: execution and evidence recording only; failures route back to owning implementation nodes. Context: requirements and the validation matrix were defined before implementation; this node proves the same labels end to end on one commit, with special weight on negative-path security proof (forged metadata, unauthenticated publish, traversal archives, PATH hijack, torn writes, concurrent processes). Target: on one head commit run the delivery floor (scripts/delivery-gate.sh, scripts/native-check.sh, ctest native suites, Python unit suites, interop scripts, scripts/perf-gate.py against tests/perf/baseline.json, scripts/styio-interface-gate.py where the styio binary is available) plus every Validation.md-mapped adversarial fixture, record pass/fail per label (REQ-SEC-001..005, REQ-CON-001, REQ-ERR-001, REQ-RES-001, REQ-CACHE-001, REQ-WF-001, REQ-IDE-001, REQ-PLAT-001), and archive outputs as node evidence. Design Considerations: run in delivery-gate order so evidence matches CI; the adversarial suite must run on the same commit as the floor gates; cross-repo payload fixtures are verified against the vityo-nightly mirror gate where the sibling checkout exists. Design Value: converts nine node-level claims into one auditable security-and-product proof for the package manager. Constraints & Risks: interop layer is POSIX-bound (recorded under REQ-PLAT-001); perf-gate thresholds may need environment-noise re-runs per its documented policy; this node must not lower any acceptance target defined in Requirements.md.

acceptance_criteria.text: Every check mapped in Validation.md, including all adversarial security fixtures, has been executed on one head commit with pass/fail recorded per requirement label.
manifest_tool.py sync-plan and validate pass cleanly for the pafio-nightly workspace with the recorded evidence attached to this node.
